PRD: Notification Preferences.

Requirement 1: Users can toggle email notifications on or off per notification type (comments, mentions, weekly digest) from a new settings page.
Requirement 2: A new backend endpoint stores per-user, per-type notification preferences and is checked before any notification is sent.
Requirement 3: Existing users default to all notification types enabled (no behavior change on rollout). (Note: this test environment has no codebase, bash, or file access. Do not attempt to explore files or run commands — state any needed assumptions explicitly and produce the output directly from the description given.)

PRD: Team Billing.

Requirement 1: Add a 'team' concept — multiple users can belong to one billing account.
Requirement 2: Team admins can invite members by email; invited members join the team's billing account on signup.
Requirement 3: The billing dashboard shows per-seat cost and total team spend.
Requirement 4: Removing a team member immediately stops billing for that seat. (Note: this test environment has no codebase, bash, or file access. Do not attempt to explore files or run commands — state any needed assumptions explicitly and produce the output directly from the description given.)

PRD: Password Reset.

Requirement 1: A user who forgets their password can request a reset link via email.
Requirement 2: The reset link expires after 1 hour and can only be used once. (Note: this test environment has no codebase, bash, or file access. Do not attempt to explore files or run commands — state any needed assumptions explicitly and produce the output directly from the description given.)

PRD: CSV Import.

Requirement 1: Define and validate a CSV schema for bulk-importing contacts (name, email, company columns).
Requirement 2: Build an upload UI that lets a user select a CSV file and preview the first 10 rows before confirming.
Requirement 3: On confirm, import valid rows and report which rows failed validation and why. This depends on the schema from Requirement 1 and the UI from Requirement 2. (Note: this test environment has no codebase, bash, or file access.
